headline: A July deadline front is turning freight speed into a proof, carton and receiving storm.
dek: The visible weather is a Drewry rate jump and early seasonal orders. The operating weather is the queue of USTR proof, CAPE refunds, packaging readiness and dock slots behind the move.

zones.name: Transpacific freight lanes
zones.operator_meaning: Drewry's 2 July WCI reached $4,530 per 40-foot container, +9% WoW; Shanghai-LA was $6,349 and Shanghai-NY $7,902.
zones.watch: Next Drewry WCI reading and whether July bookings fade after frontloaded cargo clears.

zones.name: Seasonal retail calendar
zones.operator_meaning: Retailers moved China orders four to six weeks early, while May China imports rose 35% YoY despite normal-to-soft demand caveats.
zones.watch: Retail commentary that separates demand strength from tariff hedging.

zones.name: USTR / forced-labor policy clock
zones.operator_meaning: Comments are due 6 July and hearings begin 7 July for proposed Section 301 actions, including 10% and 12.5% duty tiers plus textile/apparel mechanism.
zones.watch: Comment themes, hearing testimony and SKU/BOM exposure mapping.

zones.name: CAPE refund and finance files
zones.operator_meaning: CBP CAPE refund processing creates entry-list, liquidation-status, ACE-access and broker-authority work before refunds can become usable cash.
zones.watch: CBP's later CAPE phase and whether eligible entries convert into reliable timing.

zones.name: Carton and receiving readiness
zones.operator_meaning: Early seasonal receipts only protect service if carton specs, print approvals, pallet patterns, dock appointments and labor are ready.
zones.watch: Packaging supplier stress, corrugated lead times and DC appointment slippage.

zones.name: Food input counter-station
zones.operator_meaning: FAO's headline Food Price Index was nearly flat at 130.3, but vegetable oils rose 3.8% MoM and meat hit a record while cereals and sugar fell.
zones.watch: Category-specific input exposure; do not treat the aggregate as domestic retail food inflation.

reference_cards.label: Drewry WCI
reference_cards.note: 2 July composite, +9% WoW and +61% YoY; keep separate from other freight indexes.

reference_cards.label: Retail pull-forward
reference_cards.note: Reuters reported early China orders for back-to-school, Black Friday, Christmas and World Cup goods.

reference_cards.label: NRF/Hackett June forecast
reference_cards.note: +14.3% YoY, followed by July-September below 2025 levels.

reference_cards.label: USTR dates
reference_cards.note: Comments due 6 July; hearings begin 7 July; proposed action, not final tariff collection.

reference_cards.label: ISM customer inventories
reference_cards.note: June Customers' Inventories stayed too low; diffusion index, not a direct cost measure.

operator_translation: Run a single July deadline board by SKU: booking premium, supplier proof, product scope, carton spec, CAPE entry/refund status, receiving appointment, inventory cover and margin under the next freight rate. Assign one owner per clock before paying for speed.
operator_watchlist: Drewry's next WCI and whether Shanghai-LA/New York keep rising.
USTR comment themes and hearing testimony after 7 July.
July bookings versus NRF/Hackett's expected import air pocket.
Packaging, corrugated and warehouse stress from early seasonal receipts.
CBP CAPE phase timing and refund usability as cash.

newsletter_insert.title: Supply Chain Weather
newsletter_insert.headline: A July deadline front is turning freight speed into proof, carton and receiving work.
newsletter_insert.body: The weather map is not one blended risk score. Freight lanes, policy clocks, customs refunds, packaging readiness, receiving capacity and food inputs are separate stations this week. Drewry shows a red freight squall; USTR and CBP add policy and paperwork fronts; the carton/receiving station decides whether early orders become service protection or an internal bottleneck.
newsletter_insert.operator_translation: Before approving the next booking premium, put each exposed SKU on one board: supplier proof, carton spec, CAPE entry/refund status, receiving appointment, inventory cover and margin under the next freight rate.
